governanceNotes: Authored conservatively as ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the auriculotemporal-nerve literature classifies ATN neuralgia among the trigeminal-distribution cranial neuralgias and reviews shared anatomic territory with other trigeminal-fokal pain syndromes; classification within the same neuralgia family and occasional clinical overlap establish neither causation nor aggravation in an individual.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The auriculotemporal-nerve literature defines ATN neuralgia as a paroxysmal preauricular and temporal pain syndrome carried by a terminal branch of the mandibular (third) division of the trigeminal nerve, classifies it among the cranial neuralgias in the International Classification of Headache Disorders framework, and notes clinical overlap and differential-diagnostic proximity with other trigeminal-distribution neuralgias.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: ATN neuralgia and trigeminal neuralgia are sibling diagnoses within the same cranial-neuralgia family rather than a source and outcome, and the cited literature reports anatomic relationship and diagnostic overlap, not that one condition caused or aggravated the other in any individual.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized shared pathway has been described: ectopic firing and ephaptic transmission within trigeminal-distribution nerve fibers can produce paroxysmal neuralgic pain, and the auriculotemporal nerve carries trigeminal afferents, but a shared anatomic and electrophysiologic substrate would explain why the two syndromes resemble and co-occur with each other without establishing that either produces the other, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The literature defines auriculotemporal neuralgia anatomically, classifies it within the trigeminal neuralgia family, and reviews its differential-diagnostic overlap with other trigeminal-distribution pain syndromes; it does not establish that auriculotemporal neuralgia caused or aggravated trigeminal neuralgia in any individual. Specialist confirmation of each diagnosis, chronology, imaging, and competing explanations all require case-specific review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Neurology or orofacial-pain documentation establishing both diagnoses against accepted criteria; chronology between the two pain syndromes; imaging and examination findings (including temporomandibular joint evaluation and any vascular-compression workup); treatment-response records; competing-explanation review including post-traumatic or post-surgical neuropathy
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Classic trigeminal neuralgia from vascular compression with coincidental auriculotemporal pain
Temporomandibular disorder or myofascial pain referred to the preauricular and temporal region
Post-traumatic or post-surgical auriculotemporal neuropathy (including Frey-syndrome mechanisms) as a separate process
Persistent idiopathic facial pain or other headache disorders mischaracterized as neuralgia

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: auriculotemporal neuralgia is a sibling cranial-neuralgia diagnosis carried by a trigeminal branch, and the literature supports classification proximity and clinical overlap, not a causal relationship between the two syndromes; this edge flags the association for evidence-gap review only and must never be presented as established causation or aggravation.
evidenceGaps: Specialist confirmation of both neuralgia diagnoses with documented criteria
Chronology documenting the course of each pain syndrome
Objective evaluation (imaging, TMJ assessment, neurologic examination) excluding competing causes
A medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
